To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the low-energy expansion coefficients of two-loop supergravity scattering amplitudes in ten and nine space-time dimensions satisfy Poisson equations on moduli space and that (2) the coefficients of string theory satisfy the same Poisson equations.
the coefficients in the low-energy expansion are given by a number of SL invariant functions that satisfy a Poisson equation on the moduli space.

(1) the low-momentum expansion coefficients of the four-graviton amplitude in the toroidal compactifications of maximal supergravity are sums of SL(2,C) invariant functions of the moduli, (2) each of the SL(2,C)-invariant functions satisfies a separate Poissons equation on moduli-space with source terms that are determined by lower-order coefficients, (3) the Poisson equations have the same source terms in the toroidal and type-II string theories,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of scattering amplitudes in the low energy limit of supergravity theories.
the study of the low-energy expansion (in the momentum expansion) of scattering amplitudes in maximally supersymmetric theories in ten and eleven dimensions.
two aspects of the low energy limit of string theory: the perturbative expansion in the string coupling and the low momentum expansion of the scattering amplitudes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two-loop amplitude in eleven-dimensional compactified supergravity has the same modular structure as the corresponding amplitude in the ten- and nine-dimensional string theory, at the same level of accuracy.
the results of the paper are a striking confirmation of the conjecture that the low energy limit of string theory in ten and nine space-time dimensions is eleven-dimensional supergravity.

the results of this paper, and the previous one [hep-th/0505205], are a first step in the direction of understanding the low-momentum expansion in supergravity in the presence of supersymmetry breaking, and the relation of this expansion to the corresponding string expansion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained a set of Poisson equations for a number of SL (2, )- invariant coefficients in the low energy limit of the four-graviton amplitude in the compactifications we have considered.
the modular properties of the supergravity amplitudes can be used to constrain the string theory amplitudes.
the low-energy expansion for supergravity scattering amplitudes is a highly nontrivial function of the moduli of the internal manifold.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two-loop four-point amplitude of maximal supergravity compactified to four dimensions can be expressed in terms of a finite number of functions that satisfy a set of Poisson equations.
the low-momentum limit of the two-loop supergravity amplitude is highly constrained by supersymmetry and modular invariance.
